header.running_head: The Sahabah (RA) See Each other in their Dreams

blocks.text: (RA) then appeared in my dream and greeted me saying, 'As Salaamu Alayka wa Rahmatullaah.' I responded by saying, 'As Salaamu Alayka wa Rahmatullaah, O Abu Abdullaah. How have you found your destination?' He replied, 'It is excellent. Hold fast to Tawakkul because Tawakkul is a most excellent virtue! Hold fast to Tawakkul because Tawakkul is a most excellent virtue! Hold fast to Tawakkul because Tawakkul is a most excellent virtue!.'"[^1]

Another narration states that when Hadhrat Abdullaah (RA) saw Hadhrat Salmaan (RA) in a dream, he asked, "How are you faring, O Abu Abdullaah?" "I am well," came the reply. "Which deed did you find to be most virtuous?" Hadhrat Abdullaah (RA) asked. Hadhrat Salmaan (RA) replied, "I have found Tawakkul to be most remarkable."[^2]
Hadhrat Auf bin Maalik (RA) sees Hadhrat Abdur Rahmaan bin Auf (RA) in a Dream

Hadhrat Auf bin Maalik (RA) relates, "I saw a leather tent and a green pasture in a dream. Around the tent there sat goats that ruminated and excreted Ajwa dates. When I asked whom the tent belonged to, I was informed that it belonged to Abdur Rahmaan bin Auf (RA). We then waited for him to emerge and when he did, he said, 'O Auf! This is what Allaah has given me because of the Qur'aan. If you look yonder over that valley, you will see things that your eyes have never seen before, that your ears have never heard of and the thought of which has never crossed your heart. Allaah has prepared it for Abu Dardaa (RA) because he used to shove the world away with both his hands and chest.'"[^3]
Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Amr bin Haraam (RA) sees Mubashir bin Abdul Mundhir (RA) in a Dream

blocks.narrator: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Amr bin Haraam (RA)
blocks.text: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Amr bin Haraam (RA) says, "Before the Battle of Uhud I saw Mubashir bin Abdul Mundhir (RA) in a dream. He said to me, 'You will be coming to us in a few days.' 'Where are you?' I enquired. He replied, 'In Jannah where we are able to roam wherever we please.' I then asked him, 'Were you not killed in the Battle of Badr?' 'Yes,' he replied, 'but we were then brought back to life...'" When this was reported to Rasulullaah ﷺ, he remarked, 'Such is martyrdom, O Abu Jaabir.'[^4]
Abu Nu'aym in his Hilya (Vol.1 Pg.205).
